surprises.head: Boston kept finding open men against Charlie Lindgren
surprises.body: Lindgren allowed 6 goals on 22 shots, worth 3.0 expected goals: 3.0 more than expected, though four of them came off a pass that set up the shooter. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 35 starts.

story.head: Elias Lindholm goes off for four
paras: Tom Wilson struck first for the Capitals midway through the first, but Elias Lindholm tied it up for Boston on the power play less than five minutes later. Alex Tuch restored the Capitals’ lead shorthanded a little over three minutes later. The Bruins scored four times in the second. David Pastrňák made it 2-2 for Boston early in the second. Tanner Jeannot put the Bruins up 3-2 less than five minutes later, with Charlie McAvoy picking up his 300th NHL assist on the goal. Elias Lindholm scored again two and a half minutes later to make it 4-2, but Pierre-Luc Dubois pulled the Capitals within one on the power play just under two minutes later. Dylan Strome tied it 4-4 a little over three minutes later. Elias Lindholm completed his hat trick a little over four minutes later to put the Bruins ahead for good. Elias Lindholm added his fourth early in the third to make it 6-4, and that insurance goal turned out to be the winner. Jakob Chychrun made it 6-5 on the power play with four and a half minutes left. Fraser Minten ended any hope of a comeback with an empty-netter with a minute and a half left. Three players had three-point nights: Pastrňák with a goal and two assists, McAvoy with three assists, and Morgan Geekie with three assists.

The Capitals had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Capitals win about six in ten. Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves for the Bruins, and Charlie Lindgren allowed six goals on 22 shots. The Bruins moved to 15-7-1, fourth in the Atlantic, while the Caps dropped to 10-11-0, sixth in the Metropolitan.
